notes: This filing says: "Our standard franchise offering expects and assumes that you will operate your Franchised Business primarily from a home office." No premises rent is modeled, because a category occupancy band would invent a lease the filing does not describe. Read that sentence as written — a filing saying MOST franchisees work from home is not telling you that you will — and confirm with the franchisor what space you would actually need.

underwriting.assessment: With $250,000 liquid against a $251,428 mid-point build-out, there is a $1,428 capital gap. An SBA loan or an equity partner is required to do this deal. At mid-cohort revenue, about $48,152/mo is left after fees, rent and debt service — cost of goods and labor still come out of that, and the cash ladder below subtracts them.

financialCondition.headline: The franchisor's statements don't show the distress signals we screen for — positive net worth and a clean audit. Still worth a quick confirmation against current figures.
financialCondition.context: Worth perspective: the auditor issued a clean (unmodified) opinion and did not raise going-concern doubt; revenue is growing. We could not read usable income-statement or balance-sheet figures from this filing, so nothing here characterises the franchisor's profitability or net worth either way, including the financial-condition risk the franchisor flags about itself — read the audited statements in Item 21 directly.
body: Why it matters to you: field support, training, technology, and marketing come out of the franchisor's budget. If outside funding slows, those are the first things to get cut. There is no parent guarantee of performance in this FDD, so EverLine Holdings Aggregator, LLC is not contractually obligated to keep funding the franchisor or backing its commitments to you.

Verify before you commit: ask for the most recent interim (unaudited) financials and the current-year funding plan; ask whether the parent will sign a guarantee of performance; and cross-check Item 20 — unit closures, transfers, and terminations are the operational tell that corroborates financial stress.
aggravators: no parent guarantee backing the franchisor's obligations to you
elevated unit closures (9 in the last year, about 10% of the system)
mitigants: the auditor issued a clean (unmodified) opinion and did not raise going-concern doubt
financialCondition.evidenceNote: Flagged on the FDD's "Special Risks" page and grounded in the Item 21 / Exhibit F audited financials. Figures are extracted; all ratios and grading are computed. Confirm against the source statements and a CPA before relying on them.
